# PANCREATITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

Antimicrobials are not indicated for uncomplicated pancreatitis. In cases of necrotizing pancreatitis without infection, antimicrobial prophylaxis does not improve patient outcomes. Antimicrobials increase the risk of fungal superinfection and should not be used.

Antimicrobials are indicated for cases with pancreatic abscess, infected pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic pancreas (phlegmon). The diagnosis of infection can be difficult and may require aspiration. Consultation with Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases is encouraged.

## _______________________________________________________________________________

## Uncomplicated pancreatitis

No antimicrobials are indicated.

## _______________________________________________________________________________

## Pancreatic abscess, infected pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic

## pancreas (phlegmon)

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Total duration of antimicrobial therapy is typically 2 to 4 weeks
